$comment: The source of truth for the service marks Basalt bundles for an architecture card (DECISIONS 292, 2.4 and 2.5). One entry a mark. forms names which file draws on light grounds and which on dark ("swapped": the light file with its one fill swapped, as swap says). ink is each form's ink that meets the ground (the contrast test reads it). changes are which of 2.3's three were applied: stripped (what does not draw), fitted (the view box set to the artwork's bounds), swapped. viewBox is the fitted box per form, worked out once by fit.mjs and recorded here, so generating is the same on every machine. A mark is removed by deleting its entry and its source file; nothing else names it. Run node packages/react/marks/generate.mjs after an edit. unofficial: true marks a drawing that is not the owner's own file (DECISIONS 297: the owner asked for a mark on these even where it is not an official logo); its edits list every change made to the fetched file before the pipeline's own, and both files are in source/ with their hashes. Batch C (DECISIONS 301) added more AWS Resource icons, two Azure, three Google Cloud and Kubernetes. The floor for a multi-colour file (Azure, Google Cloud) is measured on its principal ink: the colour most of its drawing is nearest to (drawn at 128px, each opaque coloured pixel assigned to the nearest hex in the file), and where two or more are within 5 points of the largest share, the weakest of them. The file's other fills are in the owner's palette and are recorded in the entry's departures, not held to the floor, because the contrast test reads one ink a form. A legible mark whose principal ink is under 3:1 is in notShipped with its measured ratio, and comes back when the council records an exception for it.

notShipped.why: Every instance icon carries lettering that is dust at 16px (rechecked 23 Nov, Release 24-2026.07.31): Aurora's variants say "Amazon Aurora", "PostgreSQL", "MySQL", "MariaDB", "Oracle" and "SQL Server" in a few pixels, RDS says "Amazon RDS", RDS Proxy says "RDS Proxy", ElastiCache's cache node says "CACHE" and its Redis, Valkey and Memcached icons each carry one large letter (R, V, M). The one lettering-free icon, RDS Multi-AZ, draws the Multi-AZ feature, not the service. A database card takes aws-database.
Its topic and its notification icons are drawn in dotted rows that vanish at 16px (rechecked 23 Nov).

notShipped.service: AWS Step Functions, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Fargate, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon Cognito
notShipped.why: The Resource-Icons set has no icon for the service itself, and its Architecture-Service icon is a coloured tile with a white glyph (AWS's terms forbid recolouring it or removing the tile; Bedrock's tile-removed mark is unofficial, DECISIONS 297). A card for it takes no mark unless the owner asks for an unofficial one.

The only Resource icons are for a feature, not the service: EKS on Outposts and KMS's External Key Store. The Resource-Icons set has no icon for the service itself, and its Architecture-Service icon is a coloured tile with a white glyph (AWS's terms forbid recolouring it or removing the tile; Bedrock's tile-removed mark is unofficial, DECISIONS 297). A card for it takes no mark unless the owner asks for an unofficial one.
Its Resource icons are node types that carry lettering ("DC", "RA3").

notShipped.service: AWS icons with lettering in the drawing
notShipped.why: IAM MFA Token ("MFA"), Transfer Family SFTP and FTPS ("SFTP", "FTPS"), IoT MQTT ("MQTT") and Managed Microsoft AD ("MS").

marks.name: Application Load Balancer

quotes: We allow customers and partners to use these toolkits and assets to create architecture diagrams.
You can also put icons in materials like whitepapers, presentations, data sheets, and posters.
The deck in the release's PowerPoint toolkit: use the icons in a diagram at their predefined size, color, and format; do not crop, flip, rotate, or change the shape.

departures: AWS's deck says diagrams use the icons "at their predefined size", and its pages grant use in diagrams, not redistribution in a package. Basalt draws a 48px icon at 16 and ships the files (the owner's decision to bundle, DECISIONS 291).
The view box is fitted to the artwork (DECISIONS 292, 2.3), so the icon fills the 16px seat where the package's 48px box leaves about 8% clear.

marks.attribution: The Kubernetes logo is the Kubernetes Authors' artwork, used under Apache-2.0 (its logo folder offers a choice of Apache-2.0 or CC-BY-4.0: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/logo/LICENSE). Kubernetes is a registered trademark of The Linux Foundation.
departures: The CNCF publishes the icon in colour, black and white. The colour file is drawn on every ground: its blue is 3:1 or more on all of them, and the white of its wheel sits inside the blue heptagon.

Kubernetes' component icons (pod, service, deployment and the rest; github.com/kubernetes/community/icons) are not bundled: each is the same blue heptagon with a white glyph under 9px at 16, which does not tell one from another.
